newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen off, IBM to weigh on Dow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen off, IBM to weigh on Dow.

text.p: A sell-off in shares of International Business Machines Corp is expected to take the Dow industrials lower in early trading, analysts said.
But analysts said that a benign bond market and the rush of earnings reports, many of them favorable, should keep market breadth on an even keel despite weakness in blue chips.
"IBM is a major Dow component and it will hurt the average," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "Yesterday, Boeing took the Dow up, today IBM is likely to take it down."
IBM reported fourth quarter earnings per share of $3.93 compared to $3.09 a year ago. The First call consenus estimate was for $3.88.

"When you have driven a stock to new highs, hitting the consenus is not enough. The consensus number bcomes something quite ordinary," Wachtel said. Merrill Lynch cut its 1997 earnings per share estimate for IBM to $13.00 from $13.40, Wall Street traders said.
"All in all, it is not a good looking quarter. The day will continue to be dominated by earnings reports," Wachtel said.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average was up 656 points at 18,060.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was up 24 at 4195
U.S. shares in London were mostly lower.
The dollar edged up but was off its highs in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were slightly higher, with the long bond up 5/32 to yield 6.77 percent.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that some analysts are cautious about the stock of Loral Space & Communications Ltd.
Loral holders say that a large part of the stock's price is tribute to chairman Bernard Schwartz's visions of emerging satelite businesses which they don't really know how to value.
The New York Times Market Place writes that the stock of Boeing Co rose on Tuesday after the company decided not to pursue a multibillion dollar deal to build larger 747 jets.
